title: Redwood discovery - Quantumlytics latency & throughput
summary: Intro discovery focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency, and streaming token/sec benchmarking. Quantumlytics explained production use cases (customer chat, realtime alerts, summarization) with strict p95 goals and bursty concurrency. Redwood AE/SE clarified tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments, discussed batching/KV cache, quantization, and suggested a dedicated PoC benchmark with sample prompts and tooling. Next steps agreed: share pricing, security docs, and run a 2-week dedicated benchmark with Redwood support.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Alex Moreno - send tiered pricing and dedicated capacity options - due 2026-04-20
Priya Shah - share benchmark template + sample load tests and helper scripts - due 2026-04-17
Lena Cho - provide sample prompt sets and p95 targets per flow - due 2026-04-18
Mark Reynolds - confirm network/VPC requirements and region preferences - due 2026-04-19
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing + dedicated PoC proposal
Quantumlytics to share prompt sets, peak concurrency windows, and infra constraints
Schedule kickoff for 2-week Dedicated PoC (benchmarks + observability) week of 2026-04-27
Share security/compliance packet (SOC 2, ISO docs, KMS integration guide)
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (CTO, Quantumlytics), Lena (Lead ML Eng), Samir (PM)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining 
- I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick round robin before we dive?
[00:08] Mark: Yep Mark here, CTO, thanks. Big focus for us is latency and throughput for our customer chat and realtime summarization services.
[00:16] Lena: Lena, lead ML, I run the serving infra and benchmarks.
[00:20] Samir: Samir, product, I'll talk about SLAs and success metrics.
[00:25] Priya: Priya here, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll handle the deep tech bits and help with the PoC.
[00:32] Alex: Cool. High level, want to understand current stack, p95 goals, concurrency patterns, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense. Mark can you start with current infra?
[00:44] Mark: Sure. We're on GCP, running a mix of CPU endpoints for routing and GPU pool for model hosting 
- currently self-hosting a 7B LLM for assistant. We see p95 ~680ms for short prompts at low concurrency but as soon as concurrency hits 50 it jumps. We need p95 below 350ms for quick replies and sustain spikes to 300 concurrent sessions for chat.
[01:08] Lena: To add, our typical prompt lengths are 20-80 tokens, but streaming is very important for chat UI. We want token/sec targets so UX feels snappy, roughly >30 tokens/sec per stream for 1-2s initial latency.
[01:25] Alex: Got it. When you say p95 <350ms is that for 32 tokens or for full generation to N tokens? Helpful to scope.
[01:34] Samir: Good call 
- target is p95 under 350ms for endpoint-returned first chunk / initial token for streaming and p95 under 800ms for full 64-token completions non-streaming. First chunk matters for perceived latency.
[01:48] Priya: That maps to two constraints: cold path first token p95 and sustained throughput for full generation. For Hosted, we can hit lower latencies with pre-warmed pools + prefix caching, Dedicated gives more predictable throughput at scale, Private helps with network and compliance but might add some ops overhead.
[02:05] Mark: Cost is a factor. We don't want to overprovision GPUs just to hit p95. Curious about quantization and batching recommendations.
[02:12] Priya: Right 
- quantization (4-bit/8-bit) often reduces latency and memory by 20-40% depending on model. Batching helps throughput but increases tail latency if not tuned. Redwood runtime does continuous batching with dynamic batch windows to balance SLOs; KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash) for repeated prefixes cuts token generation by reusing past states.
[02:33] Lena: How deterministic is the batch behavior? We have spikey traffic aligned to business hours and sudden campaign bursts.
[02:40] Priya: We expose batching configs and autoscaling policies. For Dedicated we can reserve GPU pools and set max batch windows; for Hosted we use adaptive policies that prioritize p95 with latency-aware admission. For bursty workloads, serving a smaller model variant as fallback is supported to keep UI responsive.
[02:58] Samir: Fallback model is fine as long as we can guarantee minimal quality regression and A/B check. Also want to keep costs visible per token.
[03:07] Alex: Noted. Quick question on streaming: do you need full byte-level streaming or can you accept chunked tokens?
[03:14] Mark: Chunked tokens fine, we just need first content within that 350ms p95.
[03:20] Priya: Okay. For benchmarks, we typically run token/sec and latency sweeps: single-stream p95 at target prompt lengths, concurrency sweeps (1, 10, 50, 100, 200, 500), and mixed workloads. We'll instrument traces and token-level timings.
[03:38] Lena: Do you provide load scripts or should we reuse our existing harness?
[03:42] Priya: We'll share a benchmark template + scripts (python/locust) 
- can adapt to your harness. We'll also provide a sample prompt set.
[03:50] Mark: Network matters 
- if we do Private VPC/on-prem it might add latency. How much overhead does VPC peering add?
[03:58] Priya: Typically small, 5-20ms depending on region and routing. Private on-prem can add more depending on peering and egress. We can measure from your region in the PoC.
[04:08] Samir: Security check 
- SOC2 is required, and we need KMS integration for keys and audit logs. Any blockers?
[04:14] Alex: We have SOC2, ISO docs, and KMS/HSM integrations; we'll share the security packet. We also support SAML SSO and RBAC for team controls.
[04:24] Mark: Great. Can you summarize Hosted vs Dedicated differences for our use case?
[04:29] Priya: Hosted: fast onboarding, pay-per-use, adaptive pools; great for early testing but noisy neighbors can affect p95 occasionally. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, SLAs for latency and uptime 
- recommended for sustained heavy workloads and strict p95. Private: private control plane, VPC/on-prem options, best for regulated data but more ops. Given your p95 and concurrency targets, Dedicated PoC is the natural next step.
[04:52] Lena: For Dedicated, what's the minimum commit or pool size?
[04:55] Alex: We have entry tiers and a small dedicated cluster option for PoC. I'll send the tiered pricing. For benchmarking we can spin a pilot pool sized to your concurrency targets.
[05:06] Mark: On models 
- we're using an open 7B variant; do you validate performance across model ops?
[05:11] Priya: Yes 
- runtime selects kernels and quant profiles. We'll run quantization experiments (8-bit, 4-bit) and report perf and quality delta. Also try different compilation kernels depending on hardware.
[05:22] Samir: How do you measure p95? Is it from client request to first token or to completion?
[05:28] Priya: We measure both: first-token latency (TTFB-like) and end-to-end for N tokens. Our console gives per-route p50/p95/p99 and token-level breakdowns.
[05:36] Lena: Are there known gotchas with KV cache for short chat turns? We have many repeated system prompts.
[05:41] Priya: KV cache works well for repeated prefixes; you can persist sessions and reuse KV to reduce decode tokens. It requires session affinity or sticky routing to cache nodes, which we can configure in Dedicated.
[05:52] Mark: Any visibility on cost per token when using caching and quantization? We want to build cost models.
[05:58] Alex: We'll provide cost models showing token costs across config changes; Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quantization settings with estimated savings.
[06:06] Samir: For the PoC, timeline and deliverables?
[06:09] Priya: Propose 2-week Dedicated PoC: week 1 baseline runs (your harness + our scripts), week 2 tuning (quant, batching, cache) and final report with per-flow p95 and token/sec numbers.
[06:19] Mark: Sounds good. What's required from our side?
[06:22] Priya: Prompt sets, peak concurrency windows, region preference, any network/VPC constraints, and a contact for infra access. We'll run tests from our managed infra to your endpoints or spin a pilot cluster in your VPC depending on deployment choice.
[06:35] Lena: We'll share prompt sets and peak windows. We'll need to know if test traffic will be routed through our prod network or a test VPC.
[06:41] Priya: We recommend a test VPC for realistic network behavior with clean isolation.
[06:46] Samir: On SLA language for Dedicated, can we get p95 targets baked into contract?
[06:50] Alex: Yes, for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed latency targets and uptime clauses; we'll include sample SLA language in the proposal.
[06:58] Mark: Any rough numbers about token/sec throughput per GPU for 7B models at different quant levels?
[07:03] Priya: Roughly, on A100-like hardware: FP16 may do ~800-1200 tokens/sec per GPU depending on batch; 8-bit quant often gives 20-40% improvement, 4-bit can give more but depends on kernel support. These are rough 
- we'll benchmark your model.
[07:18] Lena: We also do reranking and embeddings. Do those share the same infra?
[07:22] Priya: Embeddings and reranking are supported; embeddings are cheaper per token generally and can be offloaded to CPU/FP32 optimized instances if needed. We can colocate workloads or separate them by route.
[07:33] Alex: Any other constraints we should know?
[07:35] Mark: Data residency 
- EU region required for some customers. Also need audit logs for access and model outputs for a short retention window.
[07:43] Alex: We support region pinning and audit logs in Console with retention settings.
[07:48] Samir: Let's recap next steps.
[07:50] Alex: Redwood will: 1) send pricing and tier options, 2) share benchmark template + scripts, 3) send security packet including SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs, 4) propose Dedicated PoC plan for week of 2026-04-27.
[08:05] Mark: Quantumlytics will: share prompt sets, concurrency windows, region preference, and indicate preferred test VPC or routing.
[08:13] Lena: We'll aim to get prompts and infra details by 2026-04-18.
[08:17] Priya: We'll set up a kickoff once we have that, and assign an SE for the PoC.
[08:22] Alex: Great, thanks all. Any final Qs?
[08:25] Samir: One 
- do you support tracing tokens back to request ids for debugging?
[08:29] Priya: Yes, we provide trace IDs and token-level breakdowns in the console and logs to correlate with request IDs.
[08:36] Mark: Perfect. Thanks, wrap up here.
[08:38] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and proposal.
[08:41] (call ends)
